result.title: Improving Character Identity Consistency in Diffusion-Based Visual Story Generation through Identity Memory and Automatic Reranking
result.comment: 12 pages, 9 figures. Project repository available at: https://github.com/MerryWex/character-consistency-visual-storytelling
result.summary: Automatic visual story generation using diffusion-based models has become an increasingly important research direction in generative artificial intelligence. However, maintaining character identity consistency across consecutive frames remains an open challenge, as existing models often produce significant variations in facial traits, clothing, visual style, or anatomical proportions. This paper proposes a modular pipeline to improve character identity consistency in multi-frame visual story generation using Stable Diffusion XL alongside additional conditioning and automatic selection mechanisms. The proposed system integrates LoRA fine-tuning for character personalization, ControlNet for pose-based structural control, and IP-Adapter for visual identity transfer. Furthermore, a reranking mechanism based on Best-of-K candidate selection and persistent identity memory is introduced to automatically select the most visually consistent generated images. The work also includes integrating and extending the StoryDiffusion framework into a reproducible local workflow, along with improvements for generated frame selection. Performance evaluation uses automatic metrics such as CLIP image similarity, DINO similarity, and CLIP text-image alignment. Experimental evaluation was conducted on a custom benchmark of multiple characters and visual stories organized into difficulty levels (easy, medium, and difficult). Both progressive variants of the proposed pipeline and extended versions of StoryDiffusion were evaluated, including SDXL baseline, Best-of-K, Identity Memory, and the Full Pipeline. Results show that reranking, identity memory, and visual conditioning reduce identity drift across frames and improve the overall coherence and stability of generated visual stories.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出一个基于 SDXL 的模块化流程，结合 LoRA、ControlNet、IP-Adapter 与持久身份记忆，并用 Best-of-K 重排序提升多帧视觉故事生成中的角色身份一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「持久记忆 + 基于 CLIP/DINO 相似度的候选重排序」可能为 LVR 的跨步状态缓存与视觉证据筛选、相似度评价提供可核查的类比，但研究对象是图像生成的帧间一致性，与推理状态生成无直接联系。
